newsitem.title: FRANCE: Twice-stolen Picasso painting recovered again.
newsitem.headline: Twice-stolen Picasso painting recovered again.

text.p: A painting by Pablo Picasso valued at up to $7 million has been recovered undamaged more than five years after being stolen for a second time, France's Grenoble Museum said on Friday.
"This is excellent news for us. The painting has not been damaged. It will soon return to the museum," said Helene Vincent, curator of the museum in the Alpine city.
The painting, entitled "L'enfant et la poupee" (Child and Doll), measures 23.3 by 31.8 cm (9.2 by 12.5 in) and was painted in 1901, during one of the master's most productive periods.
It was stolen in March 1992 and recovered by special police working for a French agency which tracks down stolen items of cultural value.
The canvas, small enough to be concealed inside a bag or a coat, was apparently stolen during visiting hours and its theft went undetected for 18 hours, museum officials said.
The circumstances of its recovery were not disclosed but investigating judge Christian Blaes has opened an investigation into the theft, museum officials said. No arrests had been made.

The painting had been stolen in August 1949 but discovered a week later. It had been taken by the director of a British fine arts school, who said he did so because he was deeply unhappy with the way it was being displayed.
